answer_1.quote: Studies have utilized natural language (NL) feedback from LLMs as descriptive guidance in editing wrong codes for code LLMs... This work aims to foster building open‑source feedback models that produce effective feedback for code editing.
answer_1.outputs: natural‑language feedback (text) describing code errors and suggested edits

answer_2.quote: The COFFEEEVAL score is defined as the proportion of test cases for which the edited code y′ produces the expected output... We also report Pass@1 scores, Pearson correlation and MSE as evaluation metrics.

answer_3.quote: We compare our COFFEEEVAL with two evaluation methods: G‑Eval and Editing. For G‑Eval, we directly assess feedback quality in Likert‑scale (1‑5) using score rubrics implemented with GPT‑4 Turbo (and GPT‑3.5 Turbo).

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation using qualified workers from MTurk. The results show that the feedback from our model is rated as more helpful and informative compared to the baselines.
answer_4.guideline: Raters score each feedback on its helpfulness and informativeness using a Likert‑scale questionnaire.
